originality.rationale: Full-text claims and equations in Lee (2003), Zhang (2010), and Levien–Bressloff (2015) were compared against the present all-cycle switching-rate zero bound and sharp reversible three-site witness. General current formulas already exist, but their inspected statements do not assert the positive-root bound or this exact reversal witness; research-record searches did not reveal an equivalent or dominating theorem. Residual possible uninspected equivalences are explicitly retained.
residual_risks: General stationary-current identities or Markov-chain tree formulas could yield the root-degree bound after additional algebra; this work does not claim those general frameworks are new.
Current-reversal literature with different indexing or inaccessible full text could contain a mathematically equivalent switching-rate root bound; Kostur–Łuczka (2001) was not read in full.
Sharpness of the cycle-size bound for n>3 is unproved and not part of the accepted claim.

value.rationale: A natural observable in reversibly flashed molecular-motor models, the oriented stationary flux, has an all-rate sign-reversal complexity bounded by spatial period. A minimal n=3 witness achieves the nonzero bound and reverses sign at a positive switching rate, despite strictly zero current in each uncoupled landscape. This is a structural transport restriction with a sharp realization, not only a computed finite example; it informs rate-controlled directional transport design.
